title: Cross-browser sign-off without a hand-run pass
lede: The checklist was empty, because nobody had time to run it by hand. Now each row names the browser tests that cover it in CI, and a Playwright script runs every row against the live app. Chrome 158 passes 29/29. Firefox 159 passes 28, and the one row the script can't check there (26) passed by hand. Nothing else was run by hand, and the script didn't run in Edge. The PR says so rather than ticking the boxes.

files.question: What has been checked, where, and how?
files.summary: One table: each user story, its automated tests, and the scripted result in Chrome, Firefox and Edge, followed by the findings.
files.owns: The sign-off a reviewer reads, and which rows rest on what evidence.
files.never: Claims a hand check it didn't get: only row 26 in Firefox is marked by hand, and the Edge column says "tests only" or "not run".
files.tested: The results are what `run.mjs` printed on 2026-11-27. The test-file mapping was checked by reading the test names.

files.question: How is each row checked?
files.summary: A plain Node script: it opens the live app in a fresh context per row, seeds the Local copy, drives the mouse and keyboard, and reads the result off the DOM.
files.owns: One `row(...)` per checklist row, the shared helpers (`open`, `drag`, `stored`, `shown`), and screenshots for the rows judged by eye.
files.never: Runs in CI or as part of `npm test`: it hits the deployed site, and the browser tests already cover the same behaviour on every PR.
files.tested: Run twice from the repo in Chrome and Firefox, with the same results each time. Lint and Prettier check it.

scenarios.name: Running one row: a drag that stops at the Board edge

steps.title: A fresh browser context with Notes already stored
steps.explain: Each row gets its own context, so no row can see another's Notes. The init script writes the Local copy before the app's code runs, so the app loads those Notes as on a reload. The `sessionStorage` flag makes the script write it only once, so a row that reloads on purpose (row 52) keeps what it typed.

steps.title: The drag stays inside the window
steps.explain: Playwright's Firefox reports a pointer outside the window as (0, −85), which threw a Note to the Board's top-left. That's the test driver, not Firefox: with the pointer kept inside the window, Firefox stops at the edge. Clamping the pointer still asks for a Note past the Board edge, because the Board is 24 px narrower than the window.

steps.title: The row compares the Preview with what was saved
steps.explain: `beforeUp` reads the on-screen rect while the pointer is still down. After release, `stored` reads the inline style React rendered from the store. Both must agree to the pixel (story 20), and the far edges must equal the Board's size (story 19).

steps.title: A row that can't be checked says so
steps.explain: Row 26 needs a pointer outside the window, which Playwright can't give Firefox. It returns `not checked`, which `row` records as SKIP rather than PASS or FAIL, so it can't pass by accident. The owner then checked it by hand in Firefox, and the doc marks that cell "✓ by hand" with finding F1.

run.to: detail: "not checked: Playwright's Firefox reports a pointer outside the window as (0, -85)",

steps.title: They see what signs it off, and what doesn't
steps.explain: The header names both kinds of evidence and their limits: tests on every PR in the real Windows and macOS browsers, and one scripted pass, not in Edge, with one Firefox row done by hand. The Edge column never shows a ✓, and the legend says what "tests only" and "not run" mean.

steps.title: They find the one design trade-off the pass surfaced
steps.explain: The script's first `ne` resize did nothing: the × sits over most of the `ne` corner handle, which the CSS comment already says. Only a strip about 2 px wide at the very corner resizes. It is listed rather than changed, because moving the × is a design decision for the owner.

run.from: **F2. The × covers most of the `ne` corner handle.**

notes.title: Not a substitute for issue #12's hand-run pass
notes.detail: #12 asks for a manual pass in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. This covers Chrome and Firefox by script, and Edge only through CI's browser tests, so the PR refers to #12 without closing it. Whether that is enough is the owner's call. Counter-argument: a script can't judge whether something *feels* right, such as drag lag or a cursor flicker.

notes.title: The script hits the live site
notes.detail: It checks what a reviewer will open, so it tests the deployed `main`, not this branch. PR #61's toolbar hint isn't live yet, and no row depends on it.
